title: With the Childlike People

teacherSummary.text: Siddhartha works for Kamaswami but treats business as a game, caring little for profit, which irritates the merchant yet makes Siddhartha successful. He watches ordinary people—the 'childlike people'—with amusement as they suffer over money and desire. Kamala teaches him the art of love, and they agree that neither of them can truly love.

vocabulary.definition: That which busies one, or that which engages the time, attention, or labor of any one, as his principal concern or…
vocabulary.context: Besides from this, Siddhartha’s interest and curiosity was only concerned with the people, whose businesses, crafts, worries, pleasures, and acts of foolishness used to be as alien and distant to him as the moon.
vocabulary.source: Webster's Revised Unabridged Dictionary (1913), public domain
vocabulary.etymology: “business”: -ness (Old English -ness, "state of"). Root not in our table: have students find it.

vocabulary.definition: The act of depositing in a store or warehouse for safe keeping
vocabulary.context: Kamaswami told him about his trade, showed him the merchandise and storage rooms, showed him calculations.

vocabulary.definition: A perennial herbaceous plant of almost treelike size (Musa sapientum)
vocabulary.context: He did not treat the rich foreign merchant any different than the servant who shaved him and the street-vendor whom he let cheat him out of some small change when buying bananas.
vocabulary.source: Webster's Revised Unabridged Dictionary (1913), public domain

vocabulary.definition: The quality or state of being hasty
vocabulary.context: But like this, I’ve had a few good days, I’ve learned, had joy, I’ve neither harmed myself nor others by annoyance and hastiness.

vocabulary.etymology: “hastiness”: -ness (Old English -ness, "state of"). Root not in our table: have students find it.

vocabulary.definition: To beset or surround with armed forces, for the purpose of compelling to surrender
vocabulary.context: But like this, Siddhartha can wait calmly, he knows no impatience, he knows no emergency, for a long time he can allow hunger to besiege him and can laugh about it.

vocabulary.definition: To roll over, or to and fro
vocabulary.context: Most people, Kamala, are like a falling leaf, which is blown and is turning around through the air, and wavers, and tumbles to the ground.

vocabulary.definition: A woman who prostitutes herself for hire

vocabulary.definition: Capable of being flexed or bent

vocabulary.definition: To warn or notify of a fault
vocabulary.context: At times he felt, deep in his chest, a dying, quiet voice, which admonished him quietly, lamented quietly; he hardly perceived it.
vocabulary.source: Webster's Revised Unabridged Dictionary (1913), public domain

vocabulary.definition: Relating to ships, their ownership, transfer, or employment

vocabulary.source: Webster's Revised Unabridged Dictionary (1913), public domain

context.history: Hesse contrasts spiritual detachment with worldly attachment, echoing Buddhist teaching on desire.

writingPrompts.label: Middle School
writingPrompts.text: In “With the Childlike People,” how does Hesse show detachment among the childlike people? Write a paragraph that states your claim, quotes two details from the chapter, and explains how each detail supports your idea. Use the characterization you noticed as one piece of evidence.

writingPrompts.label: HS Freshman
writingPrompts.text: In With the Childlike People, how does Hesse develop the idea of detachment among the childlike people? State a clear claim, support it with two or three quotations, and explain how the characterization in the chapter helps build that idea.

writingPrompts.label: HS Sophomore
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how With the Childlike People develops the idea of detachment among the childlike people. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of characterization and irony shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.

writingPrompts.label: HS Junior
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how the structure of With the Childlike People (where it begins, turns and ends) and its characterization shape the reader's understanding of detachment among the childlike people. Identify one place where the text leaves matters uncertain and explain how that uncertainty adds to its meaning.

writingPrompts.label: HS Senior
writingPrompts.text: Two readers disagree about what With the Childlike People suggests about detachment among the childlike people. Lay out two plausible interpretations, weigh the evidence for each (including the chapter's characterization and irony), and argue for the stronger one in a sustained, well-organized essay.

writingPrompts.label: AP
writingPrompts.text: Write a literary argument in which you analyze how Hermann Hesse uses characterization in With the Childlike People to complicate the reader's understanding of detachment among the childlike people. Develop a defensible thesis, select evidence purposefully, and explain how specific choices of diction and syntax create meaning.

writingPrompts.label: College Freshman
writingPrompts.text: Situate With the Childlike People within its historical and literary context and argue how the chapter's treatment of detachment among the childlike people responds to that context. Engage with at least one secondary perspective (a critic, historian or the author's own statements), integrate quotations smoothly, and cite in MLA style.

writingPrompts.label: College Sophomore
writingPrompts.text: Read With the Childlike People alongside the conventions of its genre and period. Argue how the chapter's handling of detachment among the childlike people follows or bends those conventions, using the characterization as evidence, and test your reading against one published critic. Document two secondary sources in MLA.

writingPrompts.label: College Junior
writingPrompts.text: Apply a named critical approach (for example formalist, historicist, feminist, psychoanalytic or ecocritical) to With the Childlike People and its treatment of detachment among the childlike people. State your method, show what it reveals in the chapter's characterization and irony, and identify where the text resists it.

writingPrompts.label: College Senior
writingPrompts.text: Develop a research argument that reads With the Childlike People as evidence for a larger claim about detachment among the childlike people in Siddhartha. Connect close reading of the chapter to the whole novel, engage at least four scholarly sources, and state precisely where your reading departs from theirs (Chicago style).

writingPrompts.label: Graduate / PhD
writingPrompts.text: Develop an original argument that reads With the Childlike People as a hinge in the novel's larger treatment of detachment among the childlike people. Position your reading within a named critical conversation (for example formalist, historicist, psychoanalytic, feminist or postcolonial approaches), account for the textual history where relevant, and articulate the stakes of your intervention for scholarship on Siddhartha.

satQuestions.passage: “It is very good, sir. When a person has nothing to eat, fasting is the smartest thing he could do. When, for example, Siddhartha hadn’t learned to fast, he would have to accept any kind of service before that day is up, whether it may be with you or wherever, because hunger would force him to do so. But like this, Siddhartha can wait calmly, he knows no impatience, he knows no emergency, for a long time he can allow hunger to besiege him and can laugh about it. This, sir, is what fasting is good for.”

segments.activity: Respond in writing to the bell-ringer, then pair-share.
segments.script: Settle in and write for five minutes: Siddhartha calls others 'childlike.' Is he being wise or arrogant? No wrong answers yet; we will test these ideas against the text. Two volunteers share, and I note key words on the board.

segments.activity: Introduce 5 key words: pronounce, define from context, then the word's history.
segments.script: Today's words are businesses, storage, bananas, hastiness, besiege. For each one we read the sentence, guess from context and then check Webster's. Here is the first: “Besides from this, Siddhartha’s interest and curiosity was only concerned with the people, whose businesses, crafts, worries, pleasures, and acts of foolishness used to be as alien and distant to him as the moon.” Webster's says: That which busies one, or that which engages the time, attention, or labor of any one, as his principal concern or…. Now the word history: “business”: -ness (Old English -ness, "state of"). Root not in our table: have students find it. “storage”: no root in our classroom table; have students look it up (Etymonline, OED) and record the language of origin. “banana”: no root in our classroom table; have students look it up (Etymonline, OED) and record the language of origin. Add each root to your etymology log.

segments.activity: Present the historical and literary background.
segments.script: Here is what the first readers of Siddhartha would have known. Hesse contrasts spiritual detachment with worldly attachment, echoing Buddhist teaching on desire. Why does this chapter matter? Siddhartha's superiority is ironic: he is beginning to become what he looks down on. Write down one question you want answered.

segments.activity: Teacher models a think-aloud on the anchor passage for characterization.
segments.script: Watch me read this the way a careful reader does. I read a sentence, stop, and ask what the author is doing. When I see characterization, I underline it and write in the margin what effect it has. Here I notice the diction and the sentence rhythm, and I connect them to detachment among the childlike people.

segments.activity: Read the anchor passage aloud together; annotate for Characterization, Irony, Theme.
segments.script: Now we do it together. I read the first sentence and you track along. Mark every example of characterization. Turn to a partner: what does the author want us to notice? I will collect three ideas and we choose the strongest using evidence.

I will circulate and conference.
